items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: there’s a guy named Dick Abels who was an old friend

ctx.x: I can’t remember, when was the last time we made a record for myself. But you know you’re trying to get people to buy your records. So anyway, all of a sudden calls weren’t returned and then, oh, talk to him, and then we made our way to Telarc, which will be our new home, and Telarc has Oscar Peterson and George Shearing and Andre Previn and Brubeck. And they were just like well, “make a record, go ahead, have some fun, we’ll bring your trio in and record your trio.” Great. And it’s just that I always managed to…

they stand up against all the records, I mean they’re just as good as anything that’s been made on that subject to date. They’re intelligent records. Whether or not they sell four copies or 400,000 copies, I thought they were well made, well recorded, they had a lot of class and they’re like — I have a pretty good library at RCA. And now it’s going to only get better I think. But I’ve always thought that marketability and marketing was important too, to making records. And so I’ve told RCA, I’ve told Telarc, I’m…
